clue.text: Whisky for Alfonso XIII, for one

explanation.surface: A Spanish king's favourite tipple is being chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: The American corn spirit shares its name with the French royal house, of which Spain's King Alfonso XIII was a member.

clue.text: Programme includes somewhat coarse actors

parts.note: broad humour is somewhat coarse
the cast is the company of actors

explanation.surface: A show features some rather crude performers.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio or television transmission is a show.

clue.text: At university, tense and angry

parts.note: up means in residence at university
tight means tense, as a taut rope

explanation.surface: A student is stressed and cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for irritated or anxious and hostile.

clue.text: Flatter about a hundred in the plant

indicators.note: the phrase for flatter goes round the numeral, so about shows the container

parts.note: to butter up is to flatter
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Fawning over a century of specimens in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow meadow flower is a familiar wild plant.

clue.text: Hard to abandon the recess — it's so agreeable

indicators.note: the letter for hard leaves the word for the recess

parts.note: a niche is a recess in a wall
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Leaving the alcove is difficult because it is so pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant and likeable describe something enjoyable.

clue.text: Cavalryman and strolling player, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver to say the word for a strolling player out loud and write down the word it sounds like

parts.note: a trouper is a touring actor, one of a strolling company

explanation.surface: A soldier on horseback doubles as a wandering actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier in a cavalry or armoured regiment.

clue.text: With which to torture little Tom's lot!

parts.note: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the folk tale, so little Tom's gives the surname with s
a crew is a lot or gang

explanation.surface: The tiny folk hero's companions are a means of cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval device that crushed the digits was used to extract confessions.

clue.text: Go one better than an alfresco party?

parts.note: alfresco means out of doors
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Trying to beat an open-air celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to beat a rival's achievement.

clue.text: Original explorer — one embraced by Mole

indicators.note: the breakwater word holds the number inside it

parts.note: a mole is a harbour breakwater, as is a pier
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trailblazer is hugged by a burrowing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A first settler or leader into new country is a trailblazer.

clue.text: Row in the kitchen

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out among the cooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of hills or a line is one sense; a cooking stove is the other.

clue.text: Musicians, etc, represented in Holy Writ

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the scripture abbreviation, so in marks the container here

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, part of Holy Writ

indicators.note: represented in a new form, so the letters of etc are rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians and others are depicted in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' turns ETC into CTE, which goes inside OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight players is a band of performers of that size.

clue.text: Gradual reduction of the figure essential for astronauts

explanation.surface: A shrinking number matters to people going into space.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting numbers down to zero precedes a rocket launch, and a step-by-step drop in a number is the same phrase.

clue.text: Followed closely, being obstinately determined

explanation.surface: Someone tailed another while refusing to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone like a hound is one sense; persistent and stubborn is the adjective sense.

clue.text: Antiquated — therefore permitted to be held in honour

indicators.note: the two short words are placed inside the honour, which holds them

parts.note: OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
so means therefore
let means permitted

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned is thus allowed to be respected.
explanation.walkthrough: SO and LET go inside OBE, the Officer of the Order of the British Empire award.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdated and no longer in use, as old machinery is.

clue.text: Uninspired footman

explanation.surface: A servant lacks imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and prosaic is one sense; someone who goes on foot is the other.

clue.text: Classically elegant, such a story.

explanation.surface: A refined tale is told in a classical manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic style is the pure Athenian manner; a storey at the top of a house is also so called.

clue.text: Odd device for converting motion

explanation.surface: A peculiar gadget changes one kind of movement into another.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculiar is one sense; an off-centre wheel that turns rotation into back-and-forth movement is the engineering sense.

clue.text: Boring hue disguising one close to us

indicators.note: the letters of the two words disguise the answer, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull colour hides someone nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The person living next door is near at hand.

clue.text: This paper found in a magazine?

explanation.surface: Here is an article seen in a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick drawing paper bears the name; a round of ammunition sits in a gun's magazine.

clue.text: Not a striking example of the horologist's craft

definitions.text: Not a striking example of the horologist's craft

parts.words: Not a striking example of the horologist's craft
parts.note: striking reads as a chime on the hour: a clockmaker's product that keeps time but does not strike

explanation.surface: A clockmaker's work that is unremarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or watch that does not strike is a plain timekeeper.

clue.text: Observe and record activity of the Komodo dragon

explanation.surface: Watching the giant lizard and logging its moves.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep under watch is one sense; the large lizard family includes Indonesia's giant one.

clue.text: This man may be fed in the target area

explanation.surface: Someone may be given food on the shooting range.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'inner man' is one's appetite, which gets fed; a ring of an archery or rifle target round the bull is the other sense.

clue.text: Modern look of headquarters? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the clue word reads head then quarters, and this says to put them the other way round

parts.note: N, E and W are compass quarters, north, east and west
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: The fresh appearance of a main office is questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headquarters' splits into head (NESS) and quarters (NEW); 'Just the opposite' puts quarters first.
explanation.definitionFit: Freshness or novelty is the quality of being recent.

clue.text: It can yet conceal firmness of purpose

indicators.note: the jumbled letters of the three words conceal the answer, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tin manages to hide resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Determination that does not give way is persistence of resolve.

clue.text: Good man upset about request for assignments

indicators.note: the turned letters go round the word for request
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: ST is saint, a good man
ask means request

explanation.surface: A virtuous person is annoyed about being asked for jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ST into TS, which goes round ASK.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs to be done are duties set.

clue.text: Collector's item we find strange? Not us

indicators.note: not us means the letters of us are dropped

parts.note: curious means strange
taken as written

explanation.surface: An antique strikes collectors as odd but not us.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare or unusual object is the sort of thing collectors seek.

clue.text: One demonstrating a bathroom appliance

explanation.surface: A salesperson demonstrates fittings for bathrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who displays something is one sense; the spray fitting over a bath or cubicle is the other.

clue.text: Complaint from egghead among Gort's men

indicators.note: the letter sits among the army's letters

parts.note: BEF is the British Expeditionary Force, commanded by Lord Gort in 1939-40

indicators.note: head of egg means its first letter

explanation.surface: A protest from an intellectual in a general's army.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the head of 'egg', goes inside BEF. 'egghead' wants to be a brainy person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a grievance or grumble.

clue.text: Gloomy spell in South Africa, and in the East

parts.note: a turn is a spell or stint
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A depressing time is spent in South Africa and in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullen and morose, a temper once blamed on the planet's influence.

clue.text: Mountain nymph who wore a diadem inside.

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the run of words wore a diadem

explanation.surface: A mountain spirit wears a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these were nymphs of the hills.

clue.text: Lawless extremists in Rio, perhaps, cut from 25

indicators.note: perhaps signals a possible rearrangement of the letters gathered
the extremists of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gangs of outlaws run riot in a Brazilian city.
explanation.walkthrough: L and S, the first and last letters of 'Lawless', join IN and RIO and are rearranged; 25 is BEEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime joint from the upper loin of a bullock is a cut of beef.

clue.text: Anticipate a lower-stream class, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver to speak the class name and write the word it sounds like

parts.note: a school form named 4C, the C stream being the lowest

explanation.surface: Expect a weaker school group, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools forms are named by year and stream, so 4C is a fourth-year class in the lower C stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict or see ahead is to expect something coming.
